{{Short description|American statistician and solar energy scientist}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=May 2022}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=May 2022}}
'''Eileen Clement Boardman''' ({{circa|1942}} – October 11, 2018) was an American statistician and [[solar energy]] scientist whose research included the use of statistical principles in measuring the performance of solar energy systems.{{r|obit}} She was the first woman to earn a doctorate in [[mechanical engineering]] from [[Colorado State University]],{{r|obit|stat-newsletter}} and served as president of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]].{{r|pres}}

==Life and career==
Boardman was born {{circa|1942}}, and grew up in Pennsylvania.{{r|obit}} She earned a bachelor's degree from [[Bucknell University]], and a master's degree from [[Rutgers University]].{{r|statmem}}

She was affiliated with the department of statistics at Colorado State University beginning in the early 1970s,{{r|affil}} and became an instructor for their introductory statistics courses in the 1970s and 1980s, also teaching in mechanical engineering and business.{{r|stat-newsletter}} Returning to graduate study, she completed a doctorate in mechanical engineering from Colorado State University in 1986, with a dissertation applying statistical quality measures to solar power.{{r|obit}} She became the first woman at Colorado State to earn this degree.{{r|obit|stat-newsletter}} After completing her doctorate, she became a statistical consultant,{{r|obit|stat-newsletter}} naming her firm Boardman Associates.{{r|obit}}

She survived a bout of breast cancer in 2004, and died on October 11, 2018, of pancreatic cancer.{{r|obit}}

==Recognition and legacy==
Boardman became president of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]] for 1982.{{r|pres}}

Colorado State University maintains a student award named for Boardman, the Thomas J. and Eileen C. Boardman Statistical Consulting Award.{{r|csu-award}}
